title: Decision Mesh: Low-Latency Entitlement Adapter with Incremental Audit Streams and SAML Admin Controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current RBAC runtime relies on synchronous policy lookups that increase tail latency and produce bulky audit blobs. Admin workflows (SSO/SAML) and console operations need deterministic allow/deny explanations for compliance teams. This ticket implements a Decision Mesh — a pluggable evaluation adapter that routes entitlement queries to local decision shards, supports async incremental audit streaming, and exposes explainable deny reasons and admin escalation controls for SSO/SAML-managed identities.

Goals:
- Sub-10ms median authorization checks for token-validated API calls under normal load, and bounded 95th percentile under heavy load via adaptive routing.
- Compact, incremental audit records that can be streamed to the audit pipeline in near-real time and reassembled for forensic review.
- Explainable deny metadata attached to response headers and console error UI for SREs and product admins.
- Admin escalation flow integrated with SAML attributes (e.g., is_admin override, emergency sessions) and recorded in the audit log with immutability markers.

Scope:
- Implement Decision Mesh library used by API gateway, runtime edge, and Console backend (single codebase, language: Go).
- Local decision shards with in-memory index of resolved policies + TTL-based invalidation and metrics for cache hit/miss.
- Policy dispatch rules to route to full evaluator (policy-engine service) when cache miss or for complex queries.
- Incremental Audit Stream API (gRPC) to push compact audit deltas to the audit-collector service.
- Admin escalation layer that validates SAML assertions and enforces temporary elevated entitlements with explicit audit entries.
acceptance_criteria: Authorization path library integrated into API gateway and Console backend with feature flag toggles.
Median authz latency < 10ms on internal benchmark for common token-only checks; 95th < 200ms under synthetic load profile.
Audit events emitted as compact incremental deltas and visible in the audit-collector staging dashboard; reassembly produces full event with deny reason and SAML metadata.
Explainable deny reasons surface in X-Authz-Explain response header and in Console error modal with link to audit event.
SAML admin escalation flow validated end-to-end with test SAML IdP and audit entry includes immutable escalation id and TTL.
Security review completed and threat model signed off.
Smoke tests and e2e tests for canary rollout pass in test cluster before gradual production expansion.
implementation_notes: Library (go) provides Authorize(ctx, request) -> (allow,bool,explain string, auditDeltaID string) API.
Local shard uses an LRU index keyed by (subject, resource, action, policy-version). Entries include precomputed rule matches and explain snippets.

On cache miss, a non-blocking dispatch to policy-engine via fast RPC is triggered; the library returns a conservative deny with 'pending-evaluation' tag for non-blocking callers and retries in background where caller tolerates delay.

Audit delta format uses protobuf with change-set semantics (fields: delta_id, parent_event_id, timestamp, actor, subject, resource, action, result, explain, saml_attrs, escalation_id). Stored compressed in audit-collector for reassembly.

SAML admin handling: map SAML attributes to internal admin claims at login time; emergency session handshake requires MFA confirmation and generates escalation_id tied to session token. Escalation TTL enforced by Decision Mesh shard.
Metrics exposed: authz.latency.histogram, authz.cache_hit_ratio, authz.pending_evaluations, audit.delta_rate, escalation.count. Alerts and dashboards added to staging namespace.

Backward compatibility: if feature flag disabled, calls forward to legacy authz path unchanged. The Decision Mesh library supports a compatibility shim to replay audit events into legacy storage for backfill.
tradeoffs: Cache-first approach reduces latency but risks stale decisions; mitigated by short TTLs and policy-version keys to force invalidation on rollouts.

Returning conservative denies on non-blocking misses increases false negatives temporarily; chosen to protect resources until full evaluation completes. We will provide a mode to block instead (higher latency) for admin-sensitive routes.
Incremental audit reduces bandwidth but requires reassembly for full view; audit-collector must be robust and provide tooling for reassembly for compliance teams.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Deploy Decision Mesh library behind feature flag to staging; route 1% of console traffic for shadow mode (no effect on responses) and validate audit deltas and metrics.
Phase 2: Canary: enable blocking mode for internal APIs only with 5% traffic, monitor authz failures, latency, and audit reassembly correctness for 48h.
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 25% then 75% with on-call SRE observation and rollback playbook in runbook.md.
Phase 4: Full rollout and deprecation of legacy sync evaluator after 2 weeks of stable metrics; backfill audit for previous 7 days into new audit-collector for compliance.
Rollback: feature flag kill switch and automatic fallback to legacy authz.
testing_plan: Unit tests for shard index, TTL invalidation, and explain string generation.
Integration tests: local-shard <-> policy-engine RPC correctness and failure modes (timeouts, partial results).
E2E tests: Console flows for deny/explain and SAML admin escalation with mocked IdP assertions.
Load tests: synthetic 10k rps with realistic mix of cache hits/misses to validate 95th percentile latency requirements.
Audit reassembly test harness to validate delta->event correctness under network partitions.
risks: Audit-collector availability is critical; if it falls behind, forensic queries may fail. Mitigation: short-term local buffering with backpressure and alerting.
SAML attribute mapping errors could incorrectly grant escalation; mitigation: strict mapping validation, automated regression tests, and manual approval for mapping changes.
False-denies during policy rollout could disrupt customer flows. Mitigation: conservative rollout, opt-in for customer-facing endpoints, and quick rollback path.
